translations.title: Rhyme II: An Arrow Flying
translations.text:
An arrow that flies
when shot at random,
not knowing where
it will quiver and lodge;

a dry leaf snatched
from the tree by a gale,
with no one knowing the furrow
where it will fall again;

a giant wave that the wind
ruffles and drives across the sea,
that rolls and passes, not knowing
which shores it seeks;

a light shining in trembling rings,
near to going out,
not knowing which ring
will be the last to shine;

that is what I am: I cross
the world by chance, with no thought
of where I come from or where
my steps will carry me.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXVII: How Beautiful to See the Day
translations.text:
How beautiful to see the day
rise crowned with fire,
and at its kiss of light
the waves shine and the air catch fire!

How beautiful, after the rain
of sad autumn on a blue afternoon,
to breathe in the scent of wet flowers
until one has had enough!

How beautiful, when white snow
falls silently in flakes,
to watch the restless flames
shake their reddish tongues!

How beautiful, when sleepy,
to sleep well... and snore like a church cantor...
And eat... and grow fat... and what a shame
that this alone is not enough!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXXXV: To Elisa
translations.text:
So that you might read them with your gray eyes,
so that you might sing them in your clear voice,
so that your heart might fill with feeling,
I wrote my verses.

So that they might find shelter in your heart
and you might give them youth, life, warmth—
three things I cannot give them—
I wrote my verses.

To make you rejoice in my joy,
to make you suffer with my sorrow,
to let you feel my life beating,
I wrote my verses.

To lay before your feet
the offering of my life and love,
with soul, broken dreams, laughter, tears,
I wrote my verses.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXXIV: With Their Garments Loosened
translations.text:
With their garments loosened,
their shoulders bare,
on the golden threshold of the door
two angels kept watch.

I approached the ironwork
that guarded the entrance,
and beyond the double grilles
I saw her, blurred and white.

I saw her like the image
that passes through a light dream,
like the faint, diffused ray of light
that swims among shadows.

I felt my soul filled
with burning desire;
like an abyss, that mystery
drew me toward itself!

But alas, the eyes of the angels
seemed to tell me:
“Only God may cross
the threshold of this door!”
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LII: Giant Waves That Break with a Roar
translations.text:
Giant waves that break with a roar
on remote, deserted beaches,
wrap me in your sheet of foam
and carry me with you!

Gusts of hurricane that tear
withered leaves from the high forest,
sweep me into your blind whirlwind
and carry me with you!

Storm clouds split by lightning,
their blood-red edges set aflame,
seize me in your dark mist
and carry me with you!

For pity's sake, take me where vertigo
will tear away my reason and my memory.
For pity's sake! I am afraid to be left
alone with my sorrow!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XXIV: Two Red Tongues of Fire
translations.text:
Two red tongues of fire,
clinging to one log,
that draw near and, kissing,
form a single flame;

two notes plucked together
by one hand from the lute,
that meet in the air
and embrace in harmony;

two waves that come together
to die upon a beach,
and as they break are crowned
with a silver plume;

two wisps of vapor
rising from the lake,
that join in the sky
to form a white cloud:

two thoughts springing forth together,
two kisses bursting at once,
two echoes mingling...
that is what our two souls are.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XXIX: On Her Lap She Had
translations.text:
On her lap she had
the book lying open;
against my cheek brushed
her dark curls.
Neither of us saw the letters,
I think;
but we both kept
a deep silence.
How long did it last? Even then
I could not tell.
I know only that nothing could be heard
but breath
hurrying from
dry lips.
I know only that we both turned
at the same time,
and our eyes met,
and a kiss sounded.
The book was Dante's creation,
his Inferno.
When we looked down at it,
I said, trembling:
“Do you understand now that a poem
can fit into a single line?”
And she replied, glowing:
“Now I understand!”
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XIV: I Saw You for an Instant
translations.text:
I saw you for an instant, and the image
of your eyes remained before my own
like the dark spot edged with fire
that floats and blinds one after gazing at the sun.

Wherever I fix my gaze,
I see their pupils flare again;
but I do not find you, only your gaze:
a pair of eyes, your eyes, nothing more.

In the corner of my room I see them
shine, detached and unreal;
when I sleep, I feel them hovering,
wide open above me.

I know there are will-o'-the-wisps that lead
night travelers to their deaths;
I feel myself drawn by your eyes,
but where they draw me I do not know.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LIX: I Know the Object
translations.text:
I know the object
of your sighs;
I know the cause of your sweet,
secret languor.

Are you laughing? One day,
girl, you will know why;
perhaps you suspect it,
and I know.

I know what you dream,
and what you see in dreams;
like a book, I can read on your brow
what you leave unsaid.

Are you laughing? One day,
girl, you will know why;
perhaps you suspect it,
and I know.

I know why you smile
and weep at once;
I reach the hidden depths
of your woman's soul.

Are you laughing? One day,
girl, you will know why:
while you feel so much and know nothing,
I, who no longer feel, know all.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme VIII: When I Watch the Blue Horizon
translations.text:
When I watch the blue horizon
vanish in the distance
through a veil of restless
golden dust,
it seems possible to tear myself
from this wretched ground
and float with the golden mist,
broken into tiny atoms
as it is.

When at night I gaze into the dark
depths of the sky
and see the stars tremble like burning
eyes of fire,
it seems possible to fly
up to where they shine,
to drown in their light and, blazing
with them, melt together
in a kiss.

Adrift on a sea of doubt,
I do not even know what I believe;
and yet these yearnings tell me
that I carry something
divine within me!...
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
